newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen firms as rate hike fears recede.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen firms as rate hike fears recede.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures firmed on Thursday as players ruled out a near-term interest rate hike by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) after its tankan survey showed sentiment remained wary in Japan's non-manufacturing sector.
Dealers said the market was also heartened by manufacturers' weak outlook for the next quarter's tankan, due in June.
"It's quite clear from the tankan that the outlook for June is pretty dull. So they're going to keep rates unchanged till the autumn," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.
He said the market was unlikely to be shaken even if the Federal Reserve hiked rates again in May, as is increasingly expected.
A trader with a Japanese institution said Euroyen futures rose quickly as the market reassessed the impact of the tankan, catching some players short.
But he said he remained bearish on the Japanese interest rate futures and would sell December Euroyen above its intra-day high of 99.13.
The contract was quoted at 99.12 at 1110 GMT against its IMM close at 99.09 on volume of 11,500 lots.
Japanese government bond futures for June subsided from a high of 126.88 on profit-taking to end at 126.50 against their previous 126.61.
"There were some big size sellers around 126.80 but I would still look to long these from 126.20/30," said the trader at the U.S. futures house.

He said Wednesday's news that the Ministry of Finance's Trust Fund Bureau could now hold JGBs it bought from the secondary market for five years or longer, underpinned the market as it would limit the potential supply of JGBs.
